Grounding — what the code actually says

items.value: The engine is real and proven: Barkpark.Tenancy.WorkspaceBundle (api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/workspace_bundle.ex, @canonical capability:workspace-bundle) exports a whole workspace as raw COPY dumps in a bp-export-v1 tar, with count + md5 parity tests and a partition sentinel (Catalog.assert_partition!). CLI twin: bp cloud workspace export/import (internal/cli/cloud_workspace_cmd.go), admin-gated bare routes.

THE SECRET PROBLEM IS CONFIRMED IN CODE: @pinned_e1 in workspace_bundle/catalog.ex includes api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys (per-dataset DEKs), access_grants, webhooks, share_links, registered_chat_hosts — today's bundle copies EVERY secret wholesale. Correct for backup/eject (full fidelity is the point); fatal for a dev pull. G3 is not an add-on, it is a second export PROFILE.

THE BLOB PROBLEM IS NEAR-CERTAIN: media blobs live on the instance's local disk (Barkpark.Media @upload_dir, paths like uploads/YYYY/MM/...); the bundle carries media_files ROWS only. A cross-instance import yields rows pointing at files the target does not have. G2 'verify then fix' should verify fast and spend the wave on the fix.

Import is restore-into-clean-scope, NOT a refresh: copy-strategy members (root/E1/E2) collide against existing content; only E3/allowlist members are ON CONFLICT idempotent. G1's refresh mode = route copy members through the existing temp-table + INSERT ... ON CONFLICT path with DO UPDATE semantics.

Memory risk: do_export accumulates every table dump in memory and Archive.pack returns one binary — a media-bearing or very large workspace bundle can OOM the BEAM (guerrilla is a small box). Blob transfer likely wants streaming or a sidecar channel, not naive tar members.

bp migrate already does by-id createOrReplace document copy server-to-server with a cloud-target write guard and dry-run default — prior art for refresh semantics and for the prod-write guard doctrine.
No open PRs touch workspace_bundle/tenancy/media (the concurrent gr-p4 wave is Cloud GUI settings — disjoint files). Collision risk low; surveyors confirm foreign task claims.

content.value: Direction

GROW THE PROVEN ENGINE, DO NOT BUILD A RIVAL. Wave 1 turns WorkspaceBundle from a single-purpose backup keystone into a profile-aware transfer engine, keeping the full-fidelity profile byte-identical to today. The finished experience: one command — bp cloud workspace export <slug> --profile dev --dataset <slug> — produces a scrubbed, dataset-granular bundle that provably contains zero secrets; bp cloud workspace import --merge upserts it into a scratch instance (re-run = refresh); media arrives working because blob bytes travel and re-point. The wave ends with a recorded live proof: real guerrilla dataset pulled into a scratch target, per-table count diff green, asset bytes served from the target, secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB returning zero.

items.value: G3 scrub = a dev-profile PARTITION in the catalog, enforced by a sentinel exactly like assert_partition!: every tenant table must be classified copy | deny | scrub-fields for the dev profile; an unclassified new table is DENIED and trips the sentinel. Deny list at minimum: api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys, access_grants, webhooks (or scrub signing-secret fields), share_links tokens, preview_token_jti, registered_chat_hosts, audit_events; user PII fields scrubbed. Scrub happens AT EXPORT — secret bytes never enter the artifact, fail-closed at the source.

G1 granularity = dataset-scoped WHERE clauses per partition (E1/E2 tables gain a dataset predicate where they carry one; workspace/project/dataset root rows travel minimally) + a merge import mode that upserts by primary key instead of colliding. Incremental refresh v1 = honest re-run upsert; --since only where updated_at makes it truthful.

G2 = verify the break with run output first (import a guerrilla bundle into a scratch box, request an asset, watch it 404), then fix: blob transfer as a separate streamed channel (tar sidecar or per-file fetch over the media HTTP surface, survey decides) + path re-pointing on import. Size-capped and explicitly reported — never silently partial.

Guardrails are code, not docs: import refuses prod-class targets (reuse migrate's cloud-target guard doctrine + instance Kind), pulls stay edge-to-edge (developer's bp reads source, writes target; barkpark.cloud never proxies content), provenance (source, dataset, pulled-at, scrub profile) stamped into the target.

Roster shape: 12-16 small builder tasks (catalog dev-profile partition + sentinel, export profile param, field scrubbers, dataset-granular WHERE per partition family, merge import mode, blob export channel, blob import + re-point, CLI flags, prod-target guard, provenance stamp, proof harness, secret-scan tool, docs/tests) — matching the wish for a lot more builders.

content.value: Direction debate

Candidate A — grow the bundle engine (WINNER): add profile + dataset granularity + merge mode + blob channel to WorkspaceBundle itself. One engine, one completeness proof, one format. Wins because completeness is only provable where the proof harness already lives (count/md5 parity + partition sentinel), because fail-closed scrub MUST run at the source (a client-side scrub means secret bytes already crossed the wire and sat on disk), and because every later wave (W2 snapshot/restore, G8 twin sync) wants exactly this engine — building it once here is the compounding move.

Candidate B — compose at the edge (REJECTED): leave the bundle untouched as the sacred backup keystone; build pull as a Go-side pipeline over bp migrate (documents) + schema copy + a new media sync + client-side scrub. Rejected: migrate covers documents only, so non-document tenant tables (revisions, roles, memberships, media rows, plugin state) would need a second bespoke enumeration — a shadow catalog guaranteed to drift from the real one; scrub at the edge is fail-OPEN by construction; and completeness would be asserted by hope, not by the existing parity proof. Its one real virtue — zero risk to the backup path — is absorbed by A's hard rule below.

Sharpest attack on A: you are mutating the keystone five Cloud consumers (backup, eject, rebalance, graduation, migration) inherit, and the naive blob-in-tar answer OOMs the small guerrilla box (do_export builds the whole tar in memory). Absorbed: (1) HARD RULE — the full profile's output stays byte-identical; the existing md5-parity round-trip test is the regression tripwire and profile=full is the untouched default on every route; (2) blob transfer is designed as a streamed/sidecar channel with an explicit size policy, never naive in-memory tar members — a dedicated survey question and verify target before any builder touches it.

content.value: Digest — survey round 1 (14 reports, 2026-07-19)

The direction survives contact with the code — every load-bearing claim checked out with file:line evidence, and one claim was upgraded from reasoning to LIVE PROOF: merge-import surveyor reproduced the PK-collision abort by actually running export/import twice against a scratch Postgres (duplicate key on workspaces_pkey, whole 62-table transaction poisoned — ERROR 25P02). The engine is exactly the 3-file shape assumed; do_export literally accumulates every table dump in RAM before packing; the import body is capped at 100MB server-side (workspace_controller.ex:166); the manifest tolerates additive fields, so profile/dataset ride bp-export-v1 unchanged (the format-string equality check at workspace_bundle.ex:97-99 must NOT be touched). G2 is structurally certain: blobs are disk-only (no S3/CDN backend exists anywhere), media_files carries only metadata rows, and the naive fix (re-POST via /media/upload) is WORSE than the bug — unique_filename/1 always randomizes the path, so bytes land orphaned while the imported row still 404s. G3's census is done at schema level: the deny-list is concrete, webhooks.secret is PLAINTEXT, secrets/secrets_audit only became workspace-exportable on 2026-07-17 (Connectors W21), and the big nuance is that tickets are type:'ticket' DOCUMENTS — so documents, mutation_events AND revisions all need a type-aware scrub axis, not just table-level copy|deny.

G1 is messier than the direction's 'per-family WHEREs' phrasing: FIVE distinct dataset-scoping shapes exist, and 28 of 41 E1 tables have NO dataset column at all — the majority needs a policy ruling (carry-with-workspace vs omit), not a WHERE clause. The E2 datasets extraction is also unfiltered, E3 bare-slug tables must reuse dataset_slugs_for/1's exclusivity gate, and data_keys' dataset signal is an unvalidated free-text scope string (moot: G3 denies it). Incremental honesty: hard deletes leave no trace anywhere — NO --since design can ever see them; v1 = re-run upsert only, --since deferred, delete-reconciliation (id-set diff) filed as its own future task. Prod-guard reality: NO prod-class concept exists in the codebase; bp migrate's 'guard' is a warning print behind --yes, three divergent classifiers coexist, and instance_env has the WRONG polarity (guerrilla's is nil — a 'refuse if prod' check would silently pass on the one box that matters). The guard must be a NEW server-side fail-closed opt-IN (e.g. BARKPARK_ALLOW_BUNDLE_IMPORT, default refuse) in the import controller, mirrored by a CLI pre-check. Control-plane invariant holds by pattern not rule — every transfer verb is edge-to-edge today; new transport tasks carry 'never import CloudClient' as an acceptance criterion. Provenance is fully greenfield; two homes identified (workspace.settings nested key = zero migration, vs new datasets.metadata column = matches charter's literal noun); Decide picks. Bootstrap.register_all_schemas performs a genuinely UNSCOPED cross-tenant upsert every boot that would silently revert a pulled dataset's customized plugin schemas — a real silent-failure hazard, currently code-inferred, being converted to run-proof by the verify fleet.

TWO LIVE BLOCKERS FOUND BY SURVEY, BOTH UNRESOLVED: (1) bp cloud workspace export 500s on guerrilla RIGHT NOW for BOTH workspaces — 4 reproductions, request_ids GMOxRxIEOLxbP44AAQ7y / GMOxSCzOum3k2LcAAq0B / GMOxSbrc7vaACOEAAQ8y / GMOxaEHcYh8OFewAAsUB. The catalog looks current vs the 07-18/07-19 migrations, so it is NOT an obvious repeat of the 07-15 sentinel drift; root cause needs guerrilla server logs. The crown proof is impossible until this is fixed — it gates the wave. (2) The admin CLI's -w flag is a no-op for this dataset-scoped token: -w gyldendal returns byte-identical results to -w default on dataset stats and webhook ls. Could be CLI-cosmetic (token is dataset-bound) or a genuine server-side cross-tenant scoping hole — security-severity if the latter. Both are verify round assignments with Opus.

content.value: Direction

GROW THE PROVEN ENGINE, DO NOT BUILD A RIVAL. Wave 1 turns WorkspaceBundle from a single-purpose backup keystone into a profile-aware transfer engine, keeping the full-fidelity profile byte-identical to today. The finished experience: one command — bp cloud workspace export <slug> --profile dev --dataset <slug> — produces a scrubbed, dataset-granular bundle that provably contains zero secrets; bp cloud workspace import --merge upserts it into a scratch instance (re-run = refresh); media arrives working because blob bytes travel and re-point. The wave ends with a recorded live proof: real guerrilla dataset pulled into a scratch target, per-table count diff green, asset bytes served from the target, secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB returning zero.

items.value: G3 scrub = a dev-profile PARTITION in the catalog, enforced by a sentinel exactly like assert_partition!: every tenant table must be classified copy | deny | scrub-fields for the dev profile; an unclassified new table is DENIED and trips the sentinel. Deny list at minimum: api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys, access_grants, webhooks (or scrub signing-secret fields), share_links tokens, preview_token_jti, registered_chat_hosts, audit_events; user PII fields scrubbed. Scrub happens AT EXPORT — secret bytes never enter the artifact, fail-closed at the source.

G1 granularity = dataset-scoped WHERE clauses per partition (E1/E2 tables gain a dataset predicate where they carry one; workspace/project/dataset root rows travel minimally) + a merge import mode that upserts by primary key instead of colliding. Incremental refresh v1 = honest re-run upsert; --since only where updated_at makes it truthful.

G2 = verify the break with run output first (import a guerrilla bundle into a scratch box, request an asset, watch it 404), then fix: blob transfer as a separate streamed channel (tar sidecar or per-file fetch over the media HTTP surface, survey decides) + path re-pointing on import. Size-capped and explicitly reported — never silently partial.

Guardrails are code, not docs: import refuses prod-class targets (reuse migrate's cloud-target guard doctrine + instance Kind), pulls stay edge-to-edge (developer's bp reads source, writes target; barkpark.cloud never proxies content), provenance (source, dataset, pulled-at, scrub profile) stamped into the target.

Roster shape: 12-16 small builder tasks (catalog dev-profile partition + sentinel, export profile param, field scrubbers, dataset-granular WHERE per partition family, merge import mode, blob export channel, blob import + re-point, CLI flags, prod-target guard, provenance stamp, proof harness, secret-scan tool, docs/tests) — matching the wish for a lot more builders.

content.value: Direction debate

Candidate A — grow the bundle engine (WINNER): add profile + dataset granularity + merge mode + blob channel to WorkspaceBundle itself. One engine, one completeness proof, one format. Wins because completeness is only provable where the proof harness already lives (count/md5 parity + partition sentinel), because fail-closed scrub MUST run at the source (a client-side scrub means secret bytes already crossed the wire and sat on disk), and because every later wave (W2 snapshot/restore, G8 twin sync) wants exactly this engine — building it once here is the compounding move.

Candidate B — compose at the edge (REJECTED): leave the bundle untouched as the sacred backup keystone; build pull as a Go-side pipeline over bp migrate (documents) + schema copy + a new media sync + client-side scrub. Rejected: migrate covers documents only, so non-document tenant tables (revisions, roles, memberships, media rows, plugin state) would need a second bespoke enumeration — a shadow catalog guaranteed to drift from the real one; scrub at the edge is fail-OPEN by construction; and completeness would be asserted by hope, not by the existing parity proof. Its one real virtue — zero risk to the backup path — is absorbed by A's hard rule below.

Sharpest attack on A: you are mutating the keystone five Cloud consumers (backup, eject, rebalance, graduation, migration) inherit, and the naive blob-in-tar answer OOMs the small guerrilla box (do_export builds the whole tar in memory). Absorbed: (1) HARD RULE — the full profile's output stays byte-identical; the existing md5-parity round-trip test is the regression tripwire and profile=full is the untouched default on every route; (2) blob transfer is designed as a streamed/sidecar channel with an explicit size policy, never naive in-memory tar members — a dedicated survey question and verify target before any builder touches it.

PDS Epic — Wave 1: Data Plane Honest (2026-07-19)

Living wave paper for the first bp-epic-cycle wave of the Personal Development Server epic (task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5). Charter: /papers/personal-development-server-plan (rev 3, sections 1-9 incl. the twin doctrine). Scope: G1 dataset-granular pull + incremental refresh, G2 blob/CDN re-pointing across instances (verify then fix), G3 scrub profiles (deny-by-default, fail-closed). Every claim live-proven by pulling a real guerrilla dataset into a scratch target and diffing counts: documents, assets, ZERO secrets.

WAVE STATUS: BUILDING. Decide complete 2026-07-19: 20 decisions (PDS-D1..D20) in the epic charter (durable copy .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md — the slot rotated same-day), 8 wave slices filed + published under task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5, 7 backlog tasks filed, 2 stale tasks evidence-closed. Round 1 (4 slices) builds now; rounds 2-4 dispatch after their deps merge.

The wish

"Please continue this Personal Development Server ... THIS CYCLE: PDS wave W1 (data plane honest). W1 scope per the paper: G1 dataset-granular pull + incremental refresh mode over the existing WorkspaceBundle engine, G2 blob/CDN re-pointing across instances (verify then fix), G3 scrub profiles (deny-by-default, fail-closed). Every claim live-proven by pulling a real guerrilla dataset into a scratch target and diffing counts. Guardrails: prod is never a write target; control plane keeps its no-customer-content invariant. The user wants a LOT MORE BUILDERS this wave than usual — aim 10+ builder tasks if the verified survey supports it."

Grounding — what the code actually says

• The engine is real and proven: Barkpark.Tenancy.WorkspaceBundle (api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/workspace_bundle.ex, @canonical capability:workspace-bundle) exports a whole workspace as raw COPY dumps in a bp-export-v1 tar, with count + md5 parity tests and a partition sentinel (Catalog.assert_partition!). CLI twin: bp cloud workspace export/import (internal/cli/cloud_workspace_cmd.go), admin-gated bare routes.
• THE SECRET PROBLEM IS CONFIRMED IN CODE: @pinned_e1 in workspace_bundle/catalog.ex includes api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys (per-dataset DEKs), access_grants, webhooks, share_links, registered_chat_hosts — today's bundle copies EVERY secret wholesale. Correct for backup/eject (full fidelity is the point); fatal for a dev pull. G3 is not an add-on, it is a second export PROFILE.
• THE BLOB PROBLEM IS NEAR-CERTAIN: media blobs live on the instance's local disk (Barkpark.Media @upload_dir, paths like uploads/YYYY/MM/...); the bundle carries media_files ROWS only. A cross-instance import yields rows pointing at files the target does not have. G2 'verify then fix' should verify fast and spend the wave on the fix.
• Import is restore-into-clean-scope, NOT a refresh: copy-strategy members (root/E1/E2) collide against existing content; only E3/allowlist members are ON CONFLICT idempotent. G1's refresh mode = route copy members through the existing temp-table + INSERT ... ON CONFLICT path with DO UPDATE semantics.
• Memory risk: do_export accumulates every table dump in memory and Archive.pack returns one binary — a media-bearing or very large workspace bundle can OOM the BEAM (guerrilla is a small box). Blob transfer likely wants streaming or a sidecar channel, not naive tar members.
• bp migrate already does by-id createOrReplace document copy server-to-server with a cloud-target write guard and dry-run default — prior art for refresh semantics and for the prod-write guard doctrine.
• No open PRs touch workspace_bundle/tenancy/media (the concurrent gr-p4 wave is Cloud GUI settings — disjoint files). Collision risk low; surveyors confirm foreign task claims.

Direction

GROW THE PROVEN ENGINE, DO NOT BUILD A RIVAL. Wave 1 turns WorkspaceBundle from a single-purpose backup keystone into a profile-aware transfer engine, keeping the full-fidelity profile byte-identical to today. The finished experience: one command — bp cloud workspace export <slug> --profile dev --dataset <slug> — produces a scrubbed, dataset-granular bundle that provably contains zero secrets; bp cloud workspace import --merge upserts it into a scratch instance (re-run = refresh); media arrives working because blob bytes travel and re-point. The wave ends with a recorded live proof: real guerrilla dataset pulled into a scratch target, per-table count diff green, asset bytes served from the target, secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB returning zero.

• G3 scrub = a dev-profile PARTITION in the catalog, enforced by a sentinel exactly like assert_partition!: every tenant table must be classified copy | deny | scrub-fields for the dev profile; an unclassified new table is DENIED and trips the sentinel. Deny list at minimum: api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys, access_grants, webhooks (or scrub signing-secret fields), share_links tokens, preview_token_jti, registered_chat_hosts, audit_events; user PII fields scrubbed. Scrub happens AT EXPORT — secret bytes never enter the artifact, fail-closed at the source.
• G1 granularity = dataset-scoped WHERE clauses per partition (E1/E2 tables gain a dataset predicate where they carry one; workspace/project/dataset root rows travel minimally) + a merge import mode that upserts by primary key instead of colliding. Incremental refresh v1 = honest re-run upsert; --since only where updated_at makes it truthful.
• G2 = verify the break with run output first (import a guerrilla bundle into a scratch box, request an asset, watch it 404), then fix: blob transfer as a separate streamed channel (tar sidecar or per-file fetch over the media HTTP surface, survey decides) + path re-pointing on import. Size-capped and explicitly reported — never silently partial.
• Guardrails are code, not docs: import refuses prod-class targets (reuse migrate's cloud-target guard doctrine + instance Kind), pulls stay edge-to-edge (developer's bp reads source, writes target; barkpark.cloud never proxies content), provenance (source, dataset, pulled-at, scrub profile) stamped into the target.
• Roster shape: 12-16 small builder tasks (catalog dev-profile partition + sentinel, export profile param, field scrubbers, dataset-granular WHERE per partition family, merge import mode, blob export channel, blob import + re-point, CLI flags, prod-target guard, provenance stamp, proof harness, secret-scan tool, docs/tests) — matching the wish for a lot more builders.

Direction debate

Candidate A — grow the bundle engine (WINNER): add profile + dataset granularity + merge mode + blob channel to WorkspaceBundle itself. One engine, one completeness proof, one format. Wins because completeness is only provable where the proof harness already lives (count/md5 parity + partition sentinel), because fail-closed scrub MUST run at the source (a client-side scrub means secret bytes already crossed the wire and sat on disk), and because every later wave (W2 snapshot/restore, G8 twin sync) wants exactly this engine — building it once here is the compounding move.

Candidate B — compose at the edge (REJECTED): leave the bundle untouched as the sacred backup keystone; build pull as a Go-side pipeline over bp migrate (documents) + schema copy + a new media sync + client-side scrub. Rejected: migrate covers documents only, so non-document tenant tables (revisions, roles, memberships, media rows, plugin state) would need a second bespoke enumeration — a shadow catalog guaranteed to drift from the real one; scrub at the edge is fail-OPEN by construction; and completeness would be asserted by hope, not by the existing parity proof. Its one real virtue — zero risk to the backup path — is absorbed by A's hard rule below.

Sharpest attack on A: you are mutating the keystone five Cloud consumers (backup, eject, rebalance, graduation, migration) inherit, and the naive blob-in-tar answer OOMs the small guerrilla box (do_export builds the whole tar in memory). Absorbed: (1) HARD RULE — the full profile's output stays byte-identical; the existing md5-parity round-trip test is the regression tripwire and profile=full is the untouched default on every route; (2) blob transfer is designed as a streamed/sidecar channel with an explicit size policy, never naive in-memory tar members — a dedicated survey question and verify target before any builder touches it.

Survey plan (14 assignments, in flight)

• bundle-engine-anatomy — routes, gating, Archive.pack/unpack memory behavior, format versioning headroom, existing tests. Why: every G1/G3 change lands here; memory behavior decides the blob design.
• media-blob-truth — prove/disprove that bundles move zero blob bytes; map upload_dir config, media_files.path semantics, renditions, existing media HTTP routes usable for edge fetch. Why: G2 is verify-then-fix; the fix channel depends on what HTTP surface exists.
• secret-census — every secret/PII-bearing table AND field (api_tokens hashed?, secrets, data_keys, webhooks signing fields, share_links, grants, chat hosts, tickets PII, membership emails). Why: this census IS the dev-profile deny/scrub partition.
• migrate-capability — what bp migrate covers (upsert semantics, guards, --since?), reuse vs overlap. Why: refresh semantics + prod-guard prior art.
• dataset-granularity-map — per E1/E2/E3 table: does it carry dataset/dataset_id/neither; string-vs-id duality traps; what minimal root rows a dataset-only pull needs. Why: G1's WHERE clauses are per-table facts, not a design choice.
• merge-import-feasibility — PKs/unique keys per copy-strategy table for ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE; FK ordering under replica role; what re-import into a non-clean scope actually collides on today. Why: refresh mode's core mechanism.
• scratch-target-harness — fastest honest scratch instance (bin/barkpark up, docker, ports, seed profiles) on this Mac given OOM history; CI-ability. Why: the live proof needs a disposable target.
• guerrilla-source-shape — real workspaces/datasets on guerrilla with counts (docs, media, secrets rows); pick the proof dataset. Why: the wish demands a REAL pull, not a fixture.
• prod-write-guards — existing guards (migrate cloud-target, Kind:staging, bp use --force) and where import's prod-refusal should live. Why: 'prod never a write target' must be enforced in code.
• control-plane-invariant — where a pull could accidentally transit barkpark.cloud; instance-credentials flow for a scratch box. Why: no-customer-content invariant is a hard guardrail.
• prior-art-ledger — bp papers/tasks + open PRs + foreign claims touching bundle/tenancy/media/PDS; the bp-cloud-build-charter D-numbers that bind this engine. Why: concurrent-session dup check + charter constraints we must not violate.
• provenance-stamp-surface — where target-side provenance can live (workspace/dataset metadata, settings tables) and what reads it. Why: guardrail 5 of the charter.
• schema-travel — how schema_definitions ride E1 and what a dataset-granular pull must carry for schemas to resolve. Why: a pull without working schemas is a dead box.

PDS Epic — Wave 1: Data Plane Honest (2026-07-19)

Living wave paper for the first bp-epic-cycle wave of the Personal Development Server epic (task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5). Charter: /papers/personal-development-server-plan (rev 3, sections 1-9 incl. the twin doctrine). Scope: G1 dataset-granular pull + incremental refresh, G2 blob/CDN re-pointing across instances (verify then fix), G3 scrub profiles (deny-by-default, fail-closed). Every claim live-proven by pulling a real guerrilla dataset into a scratch target and diffing counts: documents, assets, ZERO secrets.

WAVE STATUS: BUILDING. Decide complete 2026-07-19: 20 decisions (PDS-D1..D20) in the epic charter (durable copy .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md — the slot rotated same-day), 8 wave slices filed + published under task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5, 7 backlog tasks filed, 2 stale tasks evidence-closed. Round 1 (4 slices) builds now; rounds 2-4 dispatch after their deps merge.

The wish

"Please continue this Personal Development Server ... THIS CYCLE: PDS wave W1 (data plane honest). W1 scope per the paper: G1 dataset-granular pull + incremental refresh mode over the existing WorkspaceBundle engine, G2 blob/CDN re-pointing across instances (verify then fix), G3 scrub profiles (deny-by-default, fail-closed). Every claim live-proven by pulling a real guerrilla dataset into a scratch target and diffing counts. Guardrails: prod is never a write target; control plane keeps its no-customer-content invariant. The user wants a LOT MORE BUILDERS this wave than usual — aim 10+ builder tasks if the verified survey supports it."

Grounding — what the code actually says

  • The engine is real and proven: Barkpark.Tenancy.WorkspaceBundle (api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/workspace_bundle.ex, @canonical capability:workspace-bundle) exports a whole workspace as raw COPY dumps in a bp-export-v1 tar, with count + md5 parity tests and a partition sentinel (Catalog.assert_partition!). CLI twin: bp cloud workspace export/import (internal/cli/cloud_workspace_cmd.go), admin-gated bare routes.
  • THE SECRET PROBLEM IS CONFIRMED IN CODE: @pinned_e1 in workspace_bundle/catalog.ex includes api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys (per-dataset DEKs), access_grants, webhooks, share_links, registered_chat_hosts — today's bundle copies EVERY secret wholesale. Correct for backup/eject (full fidelity is the point); fatal for a dev pull. G3 is not an add-on, it is a second export PROFILE.
  • THE BLOB PROBLEM IS NEAR-CERTAIN: media blobs live on the instance's local disk (Barkpark.Media @upload_dir, paths like uploads/YYYY/MM/...); the bundle carries media_files ROWS only. A cross-instance import yields rows pointing at files the target does not have. G2 'verify then fix' should verify fast and spend the wave on the fix.
  • Import is restore-into-clean-scope, NOT a refresh: copy-strategy members (root/E1/E2) collide against existing content; only E3/allowlist members are ON CONFLICT idempotent. G1's refresh mode = route copy members through the existing temp-table + INSERT ... ON CONFLICT path with DO UPDATE semantics.

Direction

GROW THE PROVEN ENGINE, DO NOT BUILD A RIVAL. Wave 1 turns WorkspaceBundle from a single-purpose backup keystone into a profile-aware transfer engine, keeping the full-fidelity profile byte-identical to today. The finished experience: one command — bp cloud workspace export <slug> --profile dev --dataset <slug> — produces a scrubbed, dataset-granular bundle that provably contains zero secrets; bp cloud workspace import --merge upserts it into a scratch instance (re-run = refresh); media arrives working because blob bytes travel and re-point.   • G3 scrub = a dev-profile PARTITION in the catalog, enforced by a sentinel exactly like assert_partition!: every tenant table must be classified copy | deny | scrub-fields for the dev profile; an unclassified new table is DENIED and trips the sentinel. Deny list at minimum: api_tokens, secrets, secrets_audit, data_keys, access_grants, webhooks (or scrub signing-secret fields), share_links tokens, preview_token_jti, registered_chat_hosts, audit_events; user PII fields scrubbed. Scrub happens AT EXPORT — secret bytes never enter the artifact, fail-closed at the source.
  • G1 granularity = dataset-scoped WHERE clauses per partition (E1/E2 tables gain a dataset predicate where they carry one; workspace/project/dataset root rows travel minimally) + a merge import mode that upserts by primary key instead of colliding. Incremental refresh v1 = honest re-run upsert; --since only where updated_at makes it truthful.
  • G2 = verify the break with run output first (import a guerrilla bundle into a scratch box, request an asset, watch it 404), then fix: blob transfer as a separate streamed channel (tar sidecar or per-file fetch over the media HTTP surface, survey decides) + path re-pointing on import. Size-capped and explicitly reported — never silently partial.
  • Guardrails are code, not docs: import refuses prod-class targets (reuse migrate's cloud-target guard doctrine + instance Kind), pulls stay edge-to-edge (developer's bp reads source, writes target; barkpark.cloud never proxies content), provenance (source, dataset, pulled-at, scrub profile) stamped into the target.

Direction debate

Candidate A — grow the bundle engine (WINNER): add profile + dataset granularity + merge mode + blob channel to WorkspaceBundle itself. One engine, one completeness proof, one format. Wins because completeness is only provable where the proof harness already lives (count/md5 parity + partition sentinel), because fail-closed scrub MUST run at the source (a client-side scrub means secret bytes already crossed the wire and sat on disk), and because every later wave (W2 snapshot/restore, G8 twin sync) wants exactly this engine — building it once here is the compounding move.

Candidate B — compose at the edge (REJECTED): leave the bundle untouched as the sacred backup keystone; build pull as a Go-side pipeline over bp migrate (documents) + schema copy + a new media sync + client-side scrub. Rejected: migrate covers documents only, so non-document tenant tables (revisions, roles, memberships, media rows, plugin state) would need a second bespoke enumeration — a shadow catalog guaranteed to drift from the real one; scrub at the edge is fail-OPEN by construction; and completeness would be asserted by hope, not by the existing parity proof. Its one real virtue — zero risk to the backup path — is absorbed by A's hard rule below.

Sharpest attack on A: you are mutating the keystone five Cloud consumers (backup, eject, rebalance, graduation, migration) inherit, and the naive blob-in-tar answer OOMs the small guerrilla box (do_export builds the whole tar in memory). Absorbed: (1) HARD RULE — the full profile's output stays byte-identical; the existing md5-parity round-trip test is the regression tripwire and profile=full is the untouched default on every route; (2) blob transfer is designed as a streamed/sidecar channel with an explicit size policy, never naive in-memory tar members — a dedicated survey question and verify target before any builder touches it.
